subject.title: Feature: configPatch in plugin manifest — automatic config setup on install

question: Should OpenClaw add a constrained install-time plugin config-intent API, and which configuration scopes may a third-party plugin propose to change?
rationale: The core choice is whether plugin installation may alter user configuration at all; consent, allowed paths, conflict behavior, array semantics, and recovery cannot safely be inferred from the existing provider-auth patch flow.

options.title: Design constrained config intent
options.body: Add a typed, allowlisted proposal surface with visible confirmation, pre-write validation, provenance, and documented conflict rules.

options.title: Keep plugin setup explicit
options.body: Continue requiring plugin documentation or plugin-owned setup commands while preserving the current no-manifest-write boundary.

options.title: Permit broad automatic patches
options.body: Accept arbitrary manifest deep merges at install time, with the corresponding overwrite and audit risks.

recommendation.title: Design constrained config intent
recommendation.body: Add a typed, allowlisted proposal surface with visible confirmation, pre-write validation, provenance, and documented conflict rules.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue’s detailed current-boundary review and the relevant manifest/install history point to this person as the strongest routing candidate.
